clue.text: Vile celebs paid to dance

indicators.note: dancing moves bodies about, so the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneer at celebrities who will perform for anyone as long as they are paid enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vile' reads as a comment on the celebs, but it is the definition sitting at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct so contemptible or wicked that it deserves disgust; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Name a current trade hub in the Middle East

definitions.text: trade hub in the Middle East

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A geography quiz question asking you to name a modern commercial centre in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' looks like the quiz instruction, but it is a verb meaning dub; 'current' is not 'modern' but the physicist's symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf city in the United Arab Emirates is a major centre for shipping, finance and commerce in the region.

clue.text: Cry out to host possessing grooming product

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece receives another inside it

parts.note: to cry out loudly is to scream
possessing something is having it

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks at the hotel or party host who is carrying a bathroom toiletry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to host' reads as 'at the host', but it means hold inside; the containing word is split after its first letter to take the guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather spread on the face before using a razor is a toiletry used in daily personal grooming.

clue.text: Goddess lives on island

parts.note: 'he lives' can mean 'he is', i.e. exists
IS is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A goddess who makes her home on an island, as in Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the first IS sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian deity of motherhood and magic was worshipped widely throughout the ancient world.

clue.text: Solemn month

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dignified and venerable, stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: the eighth month of the year, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are spelt alike but pronounced differently, which helps hide the link.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means impressive and respected; as a noun it names the summer month after July.

clue.text: Reprimand, after 51 getting free

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
to berate someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: A telling-off comes after someone gets away with something, perhaps at level 51.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after 51' places the scolding word behind the Roman numeral, so LI comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a captive loose is to release or emancipate them, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Brown rat, I fancy, out for fish

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rodent seems to be heading out in search of fish to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like the verb 'I like', but it is the anagram signal; OUT is added unchanged at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourful freshwater species, named for its pink stripe, is a popular game and food fish.

clue.text: Advanced problem enthrals European

indicators.note: to enthral is originally to hold captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or difficulty
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A tricky, high-level puzzle has a European reader gripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advanced problem' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Technology that is cutting-edge or sophisticated is described as advanced, the informal short form of high technology.

clue.text: Enduring course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: putting up with, tolerating
second meaning: a compass direction taken by a ship or traveller

explanation.walkthrough: 'Enduring course' looks like a long-lasting class; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form means tolerating hardship, while the noun is a navigational heading measured in degrees.

clue.text: British pilgrim's Indian snack

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A British pilgrim tucks into a spicy Indian snack on the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilgrim’s' seems possessive, but the 's means 'is', joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion bhaji is a deep-fried spiced fritter served as a starter or snack in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Perhaps Murdoch's nationality, briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the novelist was born in Dublin, so her nationality is Irish

explanation.surface: A question about where a well-known Murdoch comes from, given in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the media mogul Rupert, but the definition is the novelist; the ’s means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Irish novelist Iris Murdoch wrote The Sea, the Sea, so she is one example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Split up ecstasy and rum

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A couple breaks up over drugs and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' reads as the drink, but it is the old British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people from each other so they are no longer close is to separate or divide them.

clue.text: Upset Yorkshireman resumed displaying identification online

indicators.note: to upset is to overturn, and in a down clue that turns the letters bottom to top
to display is to put on show, so the letters are on view inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A disgruntled man from Yorkshire goes back to showing his ID card.
explanation.walkthrough: Read yorkshirEMAN RESUmed backwards to find the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle a person types to log in to a website identifies them online, alongside a password.

clue.text: Principally work a long time for these?

definitions.text: Principally work a long time for these?

indicators.note: principally means mainly or at the head, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: first letter
ages is a very long time

explanation.surface: A rueful question: is pay the main reason people toil for years?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: pay is what people chiefly labour for over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular earnings received by an employee are what most people put in long hours of labour to get.

clue.text: Cake made of batter? Go on!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crisp grid-patterned batter cake
second meaning: to talk at length without saying much

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on!' reads as encouragement to try the cake, but it is a separate meaning: ramble. The word means both in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a griddled breakfast cake; the verb means to prattle or blather vaguely and at length.

clue.text: Honk horn hard in Jag

parts.note: to honk a horn is to toot it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A driver leans on the horn of a Jaguar car.
explanation.walkthrough: Jag looks like the car, but here it is a noun for a sharp jutting point.
explanation.definitionFit: A jag is a sharp projection, like the points on a saw blade or cog, each of which is a single one of these.

clue.text: Wrong of stars to have yen for model, ultimately

indicators.note: to have one thing for another is to take it in exchange, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: astral means relating to the stars
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: It is wrong for celebrities to crave being models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities, but it means the heavens. Y takes the place of the final L of ASTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Going off the correct path or into error is to go wrong, as in 'plans went awry'.

clue.text: Female with golden hair in defence

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
or is gold in heraldry
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A blonde woman stands up for herself when accused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golden hair' seems to be one phrase, but it splits in two; 'or' is the heraldic word for gold, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold is a military defence, a place built to protect against attack.

clue.text: Rejected objections in short piece

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the letters are sent back the other way

parts.note: 'ifs and buts' are objections

explanation.surface: Objections to a brief article are turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the wordplay is found in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is a short remaining end, such as a pencil stub or ticket counterfoil.

clue.text: Happiness is found in Tbilisi after odd characters expelled

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within another
throwing out the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Contentment is discovered in the Georgian capital once the troublemakers are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link verb but is a piece of wordplay, placed inside BLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect joy or complete contentment is a state of supreme happiness.

clue.text: State hesitates to dispense with borders

indicators.note: doing without borders means dropping the edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: to haver is British for to dither or be indecisive

explanation.surface: A country is reluctant to give up its frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, but it is the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly, just as one might state it.

clue.text: Buddhist monk caught pack animal

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A Buddhist monk captures a beast of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' suggests C from cricket, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is used in the Andes to carry loads, so it is a beast of burden.

clue.text: Italian food mixing air, oil and a dash of vinegar

indicators.note: mixing stirs ingredients together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, so only the leading letter is taken

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for an Italian dish that whisks air, oil and vinegar together.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a salad dressing recipe; only the first letter of vinegar goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Small square pasta parcels filled with meat or cheese are a classic dish of Italian cuisine.

clue.text: Removes water from her teddy as liquid

indicators.note: a liquid flows and takes any shape, so the letters run into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrings a soggy teddy bear dry after it has been soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' does double duty in the surface but belongs to the fodder; 'liquid' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate something is to dry it out by extracting its moisture content.
